conclusions.rationale: List order, explicit draft-only edits, one Save, restart persistence and save/discard on view switching define concrete UI transitions; stable ids and order align with the entities and Story 1.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** The settings UI lists rules in their saved order with recognized and replacement text, and supports add, edit and delete (delete asks for confirmation). Add, edit and delete change a draft; Save persists the complete rule set once; a restart shows the same rules in the same order. The list view and the bulk text view edit the same draft: switching view with unsaved changes asks the user to save or discard them first.

conclusions.rationale: Character and count limits, forbidden exchange delimiters, trimming and normalized Unicode uniqueness are explicit, measurable and shared across entry points; no external infrastructure is assumed.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** A rule is valid when the trimmed recognized text has 1–100 characters, contains no line break, tab or `;`, and does not start with `#`; and the trimmed replacement has 1–500 characters and contains no line break or tab. Recognized text is unique by its normalized key (trimmed, inner whitespace collapsed to one space, Unicode case-folded). Invalid or duplicate input is rejected with a field error and no partial write. The rule set holds at most 1000 rules.

conclusions.rationale: The six preview statuses and all-or-nothing Apply are observable; errors cannot produce a partial persisted set and the resulting set is fixed before mutation.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** The bulk editor shows all rules as text in the exchange format, accepts pasted text, and shows a line-by-line preview (add, update, delete, unchanged, ignored, error) before applying. Any error line disables Apply. Applying replaces the saved set with exactly the previewed set in one commit.

conclusions.rationale: First-tab priority and first-semicolon splitting permit semicolons in replacement text while recognized-field exclusions make serialized records unambiguous. Header, comment and blank treatment and no quoting are specified.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** The exchange format is UTF-8 text with one rule per line. A line containing a tab splits on its first tab; otherwise it splits on its first `;`. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored. The first line that is neither blank nor a comment is ignored as a header when it equals (case-insensitively, after trimming) `texte_reconnu;remplacement` or `recognized;replacement`. Export writes the header `recognized;replacement`, then one `recognized;replacement` line per rule in list order; because AC-002 forbids tab, `;` and a leading `#` in recognized text and tab in replacements, every valid rule set round-trips. Replacement text may contain `;`. CSV quoting is not supported; spreadsheet copy and paste uses the tab separator.

conclusions.rationale: Merge-by-key preserves existing positions and appends new rows; replace adopts file order. The 1 MB bound and unreadable/persistence/duplicate failure invariants make file exchange testable without cloud resources.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Import accepts a file up to 1 MB in merge or replace mode. Merge updates the replacement of rules whose normalized key matches, keeps their position, and appends new rules in file order. Replace makes the file content the whole rule set in file order. Duplicate keys inside one file or block are errors. Import is atomic: on any error, unreadable file or persistence failure, saved rules are unchanged. Export then replace-import of the same file reproduces the same rules and order.

conclusions.rationale: Unicode case folding, literal punctuation, whitespace runs, Unicode letter/digit boundaries and the per-side CJK exception fully define matching fixtures; replacement casing is preserved.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Matching is case-insensitive (Unicode case folding) and the replacement is inserted exactly as written. A match must start and end on word boundaries: the characters immediately before and after the match are not Unicode letters or digits, or are the text edges. On a side where the recognized text begins or ends with a CJK ideograph, kana or hangul character, no boundary check applies, because those scripts are written without spaces. A whitespace run inside the recognized text matches any non-empty whitespace run; other characters match literally. Punctuation adjacent to a match is kept.

conclusions.rationale: The scan order, longest normalized key, tie ordering and no rescanning are deterministic. Pipeline placement, protected approximate-correction spans, history/output parity and next-dictation activation are explicit.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Rules apply in one left-to-right pass over the final recognized text. At each position the rule with the longest normalized key wins; ties follow list order. A matched span is replaced and scanning continues after it; replacement output is never rescanned (no chaining). Rules apply after speech recognition, language detection and Chinese script conversion, and before the existing approximate custom-word correction, filler removal, normalization and AI post-processing. Approximate correction never alters a span produced by a replacement. The inserted text and the history text include the replacements. Rules committed from the UI or the CLI apply from the next dictation of the running app. An empty rule set leaves text unchanged.

conclusions.rationale: CLI parity is bounded to the existing 008 foundation and lists operations, sources/sinks, dry run, stable JSON-only output and stale-revision rejection. Dependency ownership is documented rather than implicitly introducing another CLI.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** The settings CLI (008) offers list, add, update, remove, import (merge/replace, dry run, file or stdin) and export (file or stdout) for rules, using the same validation, preview and atomic commit as the UI. With JSON output, stdout contains only JSON; errors carry stable codes and non-zero exit codes; a stale expected revision returns a conflict without writing.

conclusions.rationale: AC-001 and AC-002 exercise ordered persisted rules and CRUD confirmation; separation from vocabulary prevents conflating recognition hints with deterministic output rewriting.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Persist an ordered, uniquely keyed set of replacement rules separate from custom words/vocabulary, with add, edit, delete and confirmation in the existing settings UI.

conclusions.rationale: AC-002 defines the typed-validator predicates, while AC-005 and AC-008 propagate identical rules into file and CLI paths. The requirement is coherent with native/frontend separation.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Validate rules and rule sets with one shared typed validator (lengths, forbidden characters and leading `#`, normalized-key uniqueness, set size) used by UI, bulk editor, import and CLI.

conclusions.rationale: AC-003 and AC-004 supply explicit grammar, six line statuses and line-numbered diagnostics; BOM/CRLF handling is clarified in Edge Cases.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Parse and serialize the two-column exchange format, including header, comments, blank lines and tab or semicolon separator, with line-numbered diagnostics.

conclusions.rationale: AC-003 and AC-005 define merge/replace resulting sets and atomicity. Settings revision ownership is explicitly assigned to 008 and stale UI revision handling appears in Edge Cases.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Compute a preview (add, update, delete, unchanged, ignored, error) for bulk text and file imports in merge or replace mode, and commit the resulting set atomically with a settings revision.

conclusions.rationale: AC-006 and AC-007 cover every matching property and exact pipeline position; protected spans apply specifically to approximate correction, coherently allowing later documented normalization/AI steps.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Apply rules to final recognized text with case-insensitive, whole-word, whitespace-tolerant, longest-first, single-pass, non-chaining semantics, at the specified pipeline position, and protect replaced spans from approximate correction.

conclusions.rationale: AC-008 and Story 5 exercise all named CLI operations, dry run, validation errors and revision conflicts using the same underlying domain rules.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Expose list, add, update, remove, import (with dry run) and export operations through the settings CLI with JSON output, stable error codes and revision conflict handling.

conclusions.rationale: At least 30 table-driven cases and listed dimensions give measurable matching sufficiency, including no chaining and Unicode rather than a subjective correctness claim.

source_citations.excerpt: All AC-006/AC-007 matching fixtures pass, including at least 30 table-driven cases covering case, Unicode, boundaries, whitespace, punctuation, overlap and no chaining.

conclusions.rationale: Fixture sizes 1, 100 and 1000 and UI/CLI round-trip equivalence are measurable; ids omitted from exchange are separately documented as stable for edits, so equality refers to rules/order exchanged.

source_citations.excerpt: Export followed by replace-import reproduces an identical rule set for fixtures of 1, 100 and 1000 rules, through both UI and CLI.

conclusions.rationale: Explicit fault categories cover parse, duplicates, durable write and revision races; saved-set equality after each failure is a concrete falsifiable invariant.

source_citations.excerpt: No partial rule set is ever persisted in fault-injection tests (parse errors, duplicate keys, persistence failure, stale revision).

findings.description: The semantic spec is reviewable but explicitly supplies no READY/PASS Penflow proof; screen/mockup production remains a separate pre-code gate, not semantic approval.
findings.suggestion: Before UI code, run the required forward-contract and design gate; do not infer design approval from this receipt.

citations.excerpt: No inspection READY or certification PASS is claimed.
